races.name: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with headgear (hp) applied, winning over this exact 1m trip in Good conditions, but 47 days off and a modest recent trainer strike rate (1/19 over 14 days) raises queries about peak readiness; the key pace-setter whose fate dictates the whole race shape.

runners_data.name: Si Grass
runners_data.note: Ran second on his most recent start and has solid form over 1m in similar conditions, though his simulated-going sample is thin (1/4); Callum Shepherd can place him just off the pace and Charlie Johnston's yard is ticking at 4/33 — a quiet angle worth monitoring at a price.

runners_data.name: Luna Celeste
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with two wins from five runs on Good ground at this trip, and Daniel Tudhope's experience is a real asset in a small field; her proximity style suits a true-run race perfectly and the Clover yard is in decent form (5/14 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides for the powerful William Haggas stable (7/43 in 14 days), and Darzah has a win over this exact 1m/Good combination; the hold-up style suits a contested pace scenario ideally, though her form string (51815) shows inconsistency and she can find herself too far back if not ridden aggressively enough early.

runners_data.name: Quisana
runners_data.note: Won just 13 days ago over 1m on Good and goes handicapping in fine shape, with headgear (h) retained; the front-running role means she will burn energy fighting Two B Tanned, and while Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is firing (6/41), her lower OR of 77 is the biggest class concern against rivals rated up to 86.

races.paceDynamic: Two B Tanned and Quisana are both confirmed front-runners, meaning this 1m contest at Pontefract will be lit up from the off with a genuine contested lead on Good to Firm ground. Two B Tanned (5yo, 47 days off, headgear) has recent course-form winning over this trip in similar conditions and will want to stride on, while Quisana (last winner at 1m Good, only 13 days ago) has the freshness and proven desire to lead. The resulting honest, pressured gallop will stretch the field through Pontefract's stiff mile and is unlikely to allow either leader to coast and conserve energy, which typically burns off pace-reliant types late. This shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with tactical versatility and a potent finishing kick — specifically those like Luna Celeste and Si Grass who can track the duel without burning energy early, and a late-running profile such as Darzah who can pick up a true-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned and Quisana fight for the front and set a genuine pace, draining each other's reserves through the stiff Pontefract mile.
scenarios.body: The contested early fractions ensure the race is run at an honest clip, leaving the prominent-tracking and hold-up types with a true gallop to aim at in the straight. Luna Celeste and Darzah, both proven at 1m on Good ground with winning form, are ideally placed to finish past spent leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Quisana Controls, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Quisana (fresh, recent winner) gets the rail and Two B Tanned settles into second, leaving Quisana to control a measured pace.
scenarios.body: A calmer tempo would suit Quisana's recent winning profile and allow her to conserve enough to repel challenges, particularly if she gets a soft lead into the straight. This shape still opens the door for Luna Celeste tracking closely, but Quisana's class edge in a steadier race becomes significant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fade, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early lead battle is genuinely fierce and both front-runners capitulate inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fast-run race from start to finish compresses the field and hands maximum advantage to a strong late finisher able to sprint past the wreckage. Darzah, with Cieren Fallon and Haggas's powerful hand, is the prime beneficiary of this scenario, having proven ability to close from off the pace over 1m Good.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, Dead Slow
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits early and the pace collapses into a slow crawl with a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A bunch kick over Pontefract's rising ground would favour the sharpest accelerator regardless of usual style, potentially throwing the race open to any of the five runners. This is the least likely outcome given both Two B Tanned and Quisana have strong front-running profiles and recent evidence of pressing forward early.

watchPoints.text: Two B Tanned and Quisana — watch the first furlong closely; if both go hard immediately, the pace will be fierce and both are at serious risk of fading dramatically in the final 2f.

Darzah — Cieren Fallon must position her closer than her natural hold-up style if the field is only five runners; in a small group a true hold-up run risks conceding too much ground on Good to Firm at Pontefract.

Si Grass — limited simulated-going evidence (1/4) on similar conditions is a flag; if the ground is riding quicker than expected (going report confirms Good to Firm for this race), his exposed form may not fully represent his ability on this surface.

Luna Celeste — watch her position at the start; if she breaks cleanly and tucks in second or third behind the front-running duel, she is ideally set up to deliver her finish in the straight and her trainer's recent form supports a bold showing.

races.name: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Arabian Dusk
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo returning from 382 days off for the powerful Crisford yard, with a good second on similar going in her recent history; sits prominent naturally but the long layoff is the primary concern in a Listed contest at this level.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: True hold-up filly who has been running over 7f-8f and drops to 6f here — the trip and trainer's poor 14-day record (0/5) both work against her, and her flat-track going form (4/15 on similar ground) is thin.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a reliable placed record at this trip and going combination (five places from 15 runs on similar ground), and Ralph Beckett's yard is in reasonable form; the 7f-heavy recent profile means 6f may stretch her finishing kick slightly.

runners_data.name: Magic Basma
runners_data.note: Front-foot 4yo who races prominently and has strong placed form on good ground at 6f-7f; the 50-day break is worth noting but Kevin Ryan horses often return sharp, and Tom Eaves gets her away cleanly in most races.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride on this unbeaten-in-class 3yo who has placed in six from six on similar going — a genuine prominent racer with the highest OR among the 3yos, and a key player if she gets a smooth run from the front.

runners_data.name: Catching The Moon
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground and placed a further two times from five sim-going runs, but back-to-back disappointing efforts (13th, 12th) cloud her current form; Oisin Orr rides and she'll need early pace to bring her late run into play.

runners_data.name: Killavia
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with two wins on good ground at 5f, she has been mapped to midfield because this field has too many prominent types — her chance is materially discounted by the likelihood she cannot replicate her front-foot style here, and 6f may be stretching her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Miss Nightcap
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter with back-to-back wins and consistent placed form across all four career starts; Alistair Rawlinson knows to use her natural gate speed, and an uncontested lead on this flat 6f track is a serious advantage.

runners_data.name: Royal Fixation
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field (OR 108) with two wins and four places from six runs at 6f on similar going — K.R. Burke's yard has strong 14-day stats, and Sam James will look to slot in just off Miss Nightcap from a prominent position where Royal Fixation is most dangerous.

runners_data.name: Ruby's Angel
runners_data.note: Won over this course-and-distance profile on good ground but her last six runs show a declining pattern; naturally a prominent racer who finds herself mapped further back because of the competitive early pace picture — her chance is conditioned on getting a better draw than her redistributed position suggests.

runners_data.name: Sing The Blues
runners_data.note: Three wins from six on good ground at 6f make her a genuine competitor on form, but Martin Dunne's 14-day record (1/5) is modest and she is a natural prominent type who will be forced to race from midfield — that positional compromise is the single biggest factor tempering her win probability here.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Nightcap is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she should secure an uncontested lead through the early stages of this 6f Listed contest on good-to-firm ground at Pontefract. The field contains a surplus of prominent types — Magic Basma, America Queen, and Royal Fixation will all want to race handy, meaning a competitive early scramble for the positions behind Miss Nightcap, while Sing The Blues, Killavia, and Ruby's Angel are natural prominent racers who will be shuffled back further than they'd like. Miss Nightcap can therefore control tempo, keep it honest but not suicidal, and the race is likely to develop as a sustained-gallop contest rather than a sprint-kick affair on this flat 6f track. This shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off a controlled lead and travel smoothly — prominent types with a clean passage and genuine tactical pace, rather than true hold-up horses who need a searching gallop to get competitive. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically hold their natural positions; Miss Nightcap is almost certain to lead, with Royal Fixation and America Queen best placed to secure the prime seats behind her, while Sing The Blues, Killavia, and Ruby's Angel will be ridden from further back than usual.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Nightcap leads unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried gallop that rewards those tracking her.
scenarios.body: Miss Nightcap controls the tempo from the front, and the prominent horses who get the cleanest passage early — Royal Fixation and America Queen — are ideally placed to challenge in the final furlong; this scenario rewards horses racing in their natural style on a fair surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Heats Up Midway
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Basma or America Queen press Miss Nightcap hard from the start, lifting the overall gallop and opening the race up.
scenarios.body: A contested pace over 6f on good-to-firm ground stretches the field and brings the better-quality hold-up performers into play in the closing stages; Dash Of Azure's consistent placed record and Arabian Dusk's class profile suit a stronger-run race where finishing power is tested.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the leaders tie each other up, leaving a gap for a hold-up horse to close.
scenarios.body: Dash Of Azure or Catching The Moon, both sitting off the pace, would benefit if the prominent pack burns through their reserves; however, this scenario is tempered by the fact that several apparent hold-up positions are occupied by redistributed prominent types who lack true hold-up pedigree.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a naturally prominent horse such as Sing The Blues or Ruby's Angel manages to secure a better position than the map suggests and makes that count.
scenarios.body: Should the early traffic allow one of the displaced prominent types to slot into a handy berth, their natural front-foot racing style could prove advantageous; this scenario is low-probability precisely because the field structure makes it unlikely they can reclaim their preferred position, and their style-fit penalty must be respected.

watchPoints.text: Miss Nightcap's uncontested lead could be the decisive factor — watch whether any of America Queen, Magic Basma, or Royal Fixation attempts to press her early, as any such challenge transforms the race shape entirely.

Sing The Blues, Ruby's Angel, and Killavia are all natural front-runners who will need to settle from a wider position than usual — watch the early stages for traffic problems or rank pulling if they cannot find their stride.

Royal Fixation's OR of 108 makes her the form pick on ratings but her last two runs are below that level (7th, 5th) — watch whether she travels with her usual fluency before halfway as a guide to whether she's fully back to her best.

Dash Of Azure has been running consistently over 7f-8f and drops to 6f here — watch how she travels in the first three furlongs as a clue to whether the shorter trip sharpens or disadvantages her hold-up style.

Arabian Dusk has been off 382 days and the Crisford stable's 14-day return rate (8/24) is the best in the field — watch her market movement close to post time as an indicator of how confident connections are after such a lengthy absence.

races.name: Sky Bet Price Boosts Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: OR 91 top weight for William Haggas ridden by Cieren Fallon, confirmed front-runner who has placed at this trip and trip-adjacent distances on Good ground; blinkers fitted (hg:p), 30 days fresh, and the class edge in this field, but faces a direct pace rival in Shoof Baeed which could compromise his ability to control proceedings.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for James Owen who has placed twice over 10f on Good ground in recent runs and handles the going well (10/15 similar-going record); 15 days since last run is a positive, but needs a fast enough early pace to be generated by the two front-runners to deliver his late challenge from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Sam England's 5-year-old is in sharp form — two wins in his last five, all at 8-10f on Good ground — and his prominent racing style makes him the horse most naturally suited to tracking the contested pace set by the two front-runners; at OR 83 he is well-handicapped if running to his best recent level.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Antony Brittain who has won over 10f on Standard but has a limited record on Good ground (0W1P from 3 runs in similar conditions); Cam Hardie takes the ride and 21 days since last run is reasonable, but her going statistics give slight cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Farasi Lane
runners_data.note: 8-year-old Micky Hammond veteran who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, though the surplus of closers in this field means he is unlikely to settle as far back as he ideally wants; headgear worn (hg:p) and his single win came at 8f, making the 10f trip here a query, and his trainer's 0/3 over 14 days is a minor negative.

runners_data.name: Shoof Baeed
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3-year-old for Charlie Johnston who broke his maiden over 10f at Good and shapes as a confirmed front-runner; Callum Shepherd partners him and with only two career starts (1W1P) he is an unknown quantity under pressure — whether he can sustain his effort after contesting the lead with High Degree is the key question.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5-year-old holds an excellent record in similar going (13/15) and placed at 10f on Good recently; by nature he wants to come from behind, but the field's composition means he is unlikely to settle in his preferred rearward position, and a style-fit of 0.92 tempers confidence in his chance unless the tempo is genuinely searing.

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3-year-old has a modest recent form string (-44650) and a limited record in similar conditions (5/9); like Financer and Farasi Lane he is a true hold-up horse squeezed forward by the race shape, and his form does not suggest the class to compensate for racing out of his ideal position.

races.paceDynamic: High Degree and Shoof Baeed are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, setting up an honest, genuine gallop over Pontefract's 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground. With two willing pace-setters pushing each other, neither is likely to get an uncontested lead, which should produce a competitive early tempo that stretches the field and punishes those who are tardy into a position. This contested pace scenario typically suits horses who can travel prominently just off the speed — Jez Bomb is ideally placed to exploit that shape, whilst true hold-up horses will need the pace to be maintained deep into the straight. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Farasi Lane, Financer, and Mr Seagull are genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their natural positions given the volume of prominent runners ahead of them, meaning the race strongly favours the prominent-to-mid-division profile that can track the contested pace and strike from off the shoulder of the leaders entering the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If High Degree and Shoof Baeed push each other along at a genuine clip and the race is run to suit a stalker tracking just off the lead.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners fight it out early, burning enough petrol to leave themselves vulnerable in the final two furlongs, handing the race to the horse who has travelled smoothly just behind them; Pontefract's uphill finish rewards those who have conserved energy in transit and can produce a sustained run. Jez Bomb's recent form — two wins from five — his prominent racing style, and his excellent record at this trip and similar going make him the primary beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner establishes a clear, controlled lead early and the other fades, allowing a single pace-setter to dictate on their own terms.
scenarios.body: Shoof Baeed or High Degree gets the better of the early duel and settles into a rhythm, setting a pace that is honest but not ruinous, preserving enough energy to fight all the way to the line; at Pontefract's stiff finish a front-runner who relaxes into the lead after the initial battle can prove very hard to catch. High Degree's class advantage (OR 91) and experienced jockey Cieren Fallon give him the edge if he can secure the rail and control.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace between the two front-runners is truly severe and the field string out, leaving a gap for a closer to motor through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A truly hot tempo collapses the front end completely in the closing stages, creating a strong late run opportunity down the outside; however this scenario is tempered by the fact that Farasi Lane, Financer, and Mr Seagull are all redistributed hold-up types unlikely to get their ideal rearward position in a field dominated by prominent runners, which structurally reduces the chance of a genuine late sweep. Ammes, who has placed twice at this trip in similar going, is the most realistic late challenger.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners cut each other's throats and the race devolves into a scramble with no horse able to sustain their run to the line.
scenarios.body: An unusually messy tempo sees multiple horses weakening simultaneously in the straight, producing a compressed finish where a horse racing off a moderate pace in mid-division sneaks into a place; this shape is the least likely given the structured early pace dynamic but remains possible if the early fractions are extreme. Without Compromise, who has won at 10f on similar ground, could benefit from any positional chaos if she travels prominently enough.

watchPoints.text: High Degree and Shoof Baeed — watch the early duel between these two front-runners at the start; if neither gives way the tempo could be severe enough to compromise both their winning chances by the home turn.

Farasi Lane, Financer, and Mr Seagull — all three are natural hold-up horses unlikely to get their preferred position in a field with this much pace; watch whether their jockeys attempt to push them forward early or drop them in, as either choice carries risk.

Shoof Baeed — the 3-year-old is lightly raced with just two starts and has never faced a contested early pace; watch his behaviour in the first two furlongs to assess whether he can handle pressure from High Degree without over-racing.

Ammes — as the classiest of the genuine hold-up types, watch whether Jason Hart gets him into a position to benefit if the pace is truly honest; his two recent placings over 10f on Good suggest he is the most credible late finisher in the field if the tempo is strong enough.

races.name: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: Lightly raced nine-year-old for Michael Herrington who has won four of his last five starts on Good ground, making him an obvious live threat here — genuine prominent-running style suits the projected race shape perfectly, and Jason Hart's experience is a positive.|

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old drops back to five furlongs on fast ground having finished third last time at this trip on Good, and while Oisin Orr is a positive booking, the form string contains some inconsistency with a 'U' (unseated) suggesting temperament worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter from stall position and historical form, Dylan Cunha's three-year-old won over this course and distance on Standard and has a decent sim-going record — the key question is whether a lone lead on Good to Firm translates to enough reserve to hold on when the prominent pack arrive.|

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's six-year-old wears a visor and has an outstanding course and distance profile with four wins from thirteen runs at five furlongs on Good or similar, making the prominent position — which suits his natural style — ideal here under Cieren Fallon.|

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's visor-wearing five-year-old is a natural hold-up type but his sim-going record shows only one win from seven on comparable surfaces, and a finishing position of 12th last time out on Good ground suggests he needs more generous conditions than today offers.|

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's seven-year-old has a placed record over five furlongs on soft ground but on Good going finishes consistently mid-to-rear, and while the 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall saves some weight, the natural hold-up style needs a pace scenario that looks unlikely to materialise today.|

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' three-year-old has won twice on Good over five furlongs in recent form, showing genuine ability, but their true running style is that of a hold-up type — pressed forward onto the map by the density of closers in this field, they are unlikely to be in their optimal position and the style-fit score tempers confidence accordingly.|

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's seven-year-old blinker-wearer won over five furlongs on Good earlier in the season and arrives in fair form, but as a natural prominent racer the redistribution to midfield reflects a field where the positions close to the pace are already taken — James Sullivan will need to decide whether to fight for a forward spot or accept a position the horse is not drawn to.|

races.paceDynamic: Baker Blue is the confirmed front runner here and on Good to Firm ground over five furlongs at Pontefract, a lone pace-setter who goes unchallenged from the front is an enviable position — they will dictate a clean, even gallop without being pressured into unsustainable splits. Badri, Fluorescence, and Rocking Ends will press forward into prominent positions just off the lead, creating a well-organised pack that largely tracks Baker Blue through the early stages without anyone firing the race up into a sprint. This field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Reigning Profit, a genuine hold-up horse pushed to midfield on the map, and One And Gone, a true closer also redistributed forward, are both racing out of their optimal roles, meaning the front-to-midfield cluster is effectively compressed. The race shape strongly favours horses racing close to a sustainable, uncontested pace — prominent-to-lead types who can travel comfortably and produce a finishing effort in the final furlong rather than needing a true pace collapse to arrive late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Baker Blue dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent pack track without drama.
scenarios.body: Baker Blue sets a measured tempo on ground that suits, and the horses sitting just behind — Badri and Rocking Ends — travel into the race before being asked for their effort inside the final furlong; with no pace collapse there is no room for closers to overhaul them. Prominent horses with proven form on Good going at five furlongs receive the clearest conditions here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough that the lead horse ties up in the final 100 yards and the prominent trackers sweep past in a group.
scenarios.body: Baker Blue has burned enough petrol holding the lead that the closing stages see Badri, Fluorescence, or Rocking Ends — all sitting a length or two off — accelerate past cleanly, making the final furlong a battle between prominent types rather than between front and held-up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and create genuine late ground for a closer.
scenarios.body: Vintage Clarets or Kylian, racing from the rear of the main group, would need those in front to have posted a genuinely taxing early pace — a scenario complicated by One And Gone and Reigning Profit being out of their natural hold-up roles and unlikely to be delivering true late runs. The style-fit discounts on both redistributed closers reduce confidence that a genuine finishing burst arrives in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group race too keenly early and the whole front section fades entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An unlikely scenario given Baker Blue's uncontested lead — there is no rival forcing a pace duel to create genuine pressure — but if the Good to Firm ground produces unusually fast early splits and Baker Blue's rivals press harder than expected, any horse conserving energy from mid to rear could potentially pick up the pieces. Reigning Profit and One And Gone, despite being redistributed and racing out of role, would theoretically benefit if the front runners tied up entirely, though their positional disadvantage makes this genuinely hard to execute.

watchPoints.text: Baker Blue to track in the early strides — if any of Badri, Rocking Ends or Fluorescence press harder than expected and force a contested lead, the pace dynamic changes completely and the hold-up horses become more viable.

One And Gone and Reigning Profit are both racing out of their natural roles; watch the initial break and first two furlongs to see whether either secures a more forward position than the pace map suggests — if they do, their form figures become more relevant.

Rocking Ends has the most consistent Good-ground five-furlong course form of any horse in the race — if Cieren Fallon slots in just off the pace cleanly and Baker Blue leads at a modest tempo, the combination of proven conditions and prominent style makes this horse unusually dangerous in scenario A.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm for the 5:45, faster than some of the sim-going records suggest — Kylian and Vintage Clarets both carry concerned recent finishing positions on Good and the extra pace of this surface may stretch them further than the raw OR gap implies.

races.name: Sky Bet Extra Places Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with solid Good-ground form (13/15 positional finishes), but an OR of 84 is the highest in the race and Charlie Johnston's 14-day strike rate of 4/33 is modest; only 8 days since last run is a slight positive for freshness, though he has failed to win in six recent starts.

runners_data.name: Laafy
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old wearing a visor and returning from 50 days off, with Brian Ellison's stable at 3/20 in the 14-day window; his recent form figures of 08-00 are concerning and his similar-going record (7/15) is the weakest in the field, making him a significant risk at this trip and going combination.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old comes back from 57 days off with three wins from her last five starts, two of them on Good ground, and holds potential as a hold-up runner who could exploit a genuine gallop set by the front pair; Lauren Young's 5lb claim brings the weight down further, though Goldie's 14-day strike rate of 3/43 invites caution.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Hat-trick seeking front-runner with exceptional Good-ground form (13/15, 7 wins) and an in-form handler at 9/46 in the 14-day window; Cieren Fallon rides and will look to replicate the dictating front-running tactics that have won three consecutive races, though now steps up significantly to 2m1f and faces a direct lead rival in Treasure Islands.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins over 2m-plus trips on Good going but recent form has dipped (7th, 6th, 12th before those wins); Tim Easterby's runner will dispute the pace with Sixty Plus throughout, and the energy cost of that battle over this marathon trip is a real concern for his finishing position.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old arrives on a hat-trick of wins including two at 2m on Good ground, carries the lowest weight at 120lbs, and has a proven record at the trip; the hold-up style and Prescott's renowned placing acumen make her a potent closer if the front-runners burn each other out, though her similar-going sample is small (2/7).

races.paceDynamic: Sixty Plus and Treasure Islands are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the jump over this 2m1f trip at Pontefract on Good to Firm ground, creating an honest, competitive gallop rather than a dawdle. Sixty Plus arrives on a hat-trick of wins, all front-led, and jockey Cieren Fallon will be keen to replicate that pattern; Treasure Islands won over 2m at this trip-range and will not surrender the rail without a fight, meaning neither will get a soft lead. The resulting pace is likely to be genuine throughout, potentially injecting pressure across the whole field rather than building to a single explosive finish. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or hold-up horse who settles behind a genuine gallop and finishes with purpose — specifically pointing toward Campeona and Letsbefrank, both of whom possess late-run profiles and are capable of exploiting front-runners who have burned energy battling for the lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Front Pair
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus and Treasure Islands fight for supremacy and set a true honest gallop that depletes both before the straight.
scenarios.body: The two lead rivals push each other along throughout the extended 2m1f trip, leaving the prominent and hold-up horses travelling comfortably behind before asserting in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sixty Plus Controls and Kicks
scenarios.trigger: If Treasure Islands concedes the lead early and Sixty Plus is allowed to dictate a measured tempo unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Sixty Plus, in blistering recent form with three consecutive wins all front-led, settles into a rhythm and finds enough reserves to repel challenges in the straight; his Good to Firm record (13/15 positional finishes) underlines this track-condition suitability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough throughout that even the prominent runners tire, leaving a hold-up horse to pick up the pieces deep inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Letsbefrank, who has won three of her last five starts including at shorter trips on Good, would have the stamina and finishing resolve to reel in weakening rivals; Campeona's hat-trick form and Sir Mark Prescott's placement instinct make her equally dangerous in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits early and the pace collapses into a falsely run affair that suits a closer who adapts.
scenarios.body: A slow early fractions scenario over this long trip is unlikely given both Sixty Plus and Treasure Islands have strong front-running profiles, but if it occurs the race becomes a sprint-style finish where Campeona's recent class and three-year-old weight advantage could be decisive.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sixty Plus and Treasure Islands in the first half-mile — if both are hard at it for the lead before the field settles, the pace will be genuinely hot and front-runners should be opposed at the finish.

Campeona is unbeaten in three runs at 2m-plus and Prescott rarely runs horses out of their comfort zone; if she travels smoothly in behind, she is a significant danger to any leader who has expended energy in a battle.

Letsbefrank is 57 days off the track with a trainer (Jim Goldie) who runs at a low 14-day strike rate; her fitness level should be watched in the paddock before committing to her chance in the scenario where closing form is required.

Treasure Islands has placed at 2m-plus on Good but her last three runs produced a 7th, 6th, and 12th — if she is in a true lead battle, she may fade significantly before the straight, altering the race shape entirely.

Laafy (visor, 50 days off, age 10) looks the most vulnerable on form and going stats and is worth monitoring purely for whether he absorbs early pace pressure or is dropped out, as his positioning could affect how hard Sixty Plus has to work if Treasure Islands softens early.

races.name: Sky Bet Proud To Support Young Lives Vs Cancer Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner here; Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for David O'Meara's in-form yard (9/51 in 14 days) and she returns after 22 days to a trip and going combination where she has finished in the frame multiple times — her uncontested lead is the defining feature of this race shape, though the STYLE_FIT tag signals a slight positional stretch.

runners_data.name: Alfa Whiteburd
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins heading into this, including two over 6f on good ground, and Jason Hart's course familiarity adds confidence; Ivan Furtado's yard has struck at 1/15 in the last fortnight and this mare carries strong recent momentum, though she will need to find clear air from the hold-up pack to deliver another winning effort.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has saddled three winners from 28 runners in the last 14 days and Cieren Fallon is an astute appointment; the form line includes a 7f soft-ground win and a 6f placed effort on standard going, and the hood (headgear flagged) could sharpen her response, though the 37-day absence is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Russet Gold
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's six-year-old has posted five consecutive placed or beaten efforts at 6f on good ground without winning, and Tom Eaves picks up the ride; a true hold-up specialist whose recent form at this trip suggests consistency without the final kick — placed in the map against her natural rear position because the field's hold-up contingent is simply too large to all sit where they want.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 6f on good ground at this very course and wearing a visor, David O'Meara's four-year-old has strong course-and-distance placed form and returns after the same 22-day break as stablemate Veblen Good; Mark Winn navigates from a hold-up berth and will need a clean run through the congested late runners.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old arrives in excellent heart after back-to-back wins at 6f on good ground, with Joanna Mason maintaining the partnership; racing prominently is her natural mode and in a race where only Veblen Good leads, she can tuck in second and mount her challenge without burning unnecessary energy — structurally very well placed.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Ethan Tindall claims 5lb for Richard and Peter Fahey's yard, which has returned 4/29 recently; the six-year-old has placed form on 6f good ground including two thirds, but the form string tails off and the hold-up style means he is competing with several similar runners for the same late ground — the field's depth at the rear limits his opportunity.

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's nine-year-old has been campaigned predominantly at 5f of late and steps back up to 6f, which adds a question mark over whether the extra furlong suits at this stage of his career; Cam Hardie takes the ride and a placed effort at 5f on good suggests he retains some ability, but the step up in trip combined with the congested hold-up scenario makes him among the more vulnerable runners here.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: James Sullivan partners Ruth Carr's second runner and the form string contains a win and multiple placed efforts at 6f on good ground, showing the trip and conditions suit; the 9-day turnaround is quick but the yard has been active, and while his hold-up style is genuine, he faces the same traffic risks as all the rear-group runners in what is a deeply congested finishing pack.

races.paceDynamic: Veblen Good is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Pontefract, and with no genuine rival looking to contest the lead, she is set to dictate from the gates at a controlled, sustainable tempo. The Good Biscuit is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely settle just off the pace behind Veblen Good, creating a small lead group of two ahead of a dense bunch of hold-up types. The bulk of the field — Alfa Whiteburd, Rare Change, Yes I'm Mali, Russet Gold, Havana Rum, Mondammej and Fiscal Policy — are all natural hold-up horses, meaning the rear of the field will be congested and finishing runs will be launched from similar positions. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace at a measured gallop, as a single front-runner setting an uncontested tempo at Pontefract over 6f hands a significant structural advantage to Veblen Good and The Good Biscuit; the field holds far more hold-up types than the track can reward, with Russet Gold, Havana Rum, Mondammej and Fiscal Policy all mapped forward of their true position because the rear is simply too congested for the map to place them all there.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Veblen Good Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good breaks cleanly and sets a measured, uncontested pace throughout the 6f trip.
scenarios.body: Veblen Good dictates from the front at a tempo that suits her, never coming under pressure until the final furlong where her good-to-firm form and comfortable position tell; The Good Biscuit, tracking just off the pace, is the main beneficiary of the shape and can chase the leader home without burning energy in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Storm
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good's tempo is slightly higher than ideal, opening the door for late closers to mow her down.
scenarios.body: A brisk but not blistering pace from Veblen Good provides enough early cover for the genuine hold-up horses to find clear air in the straight; Alfa Whiteburd, in red-hot form with three recent wins, and Yes I'm Mali, who has placed twice on this track at this trip, are best positioned to benefit from a strong finishing run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good goes too slow and the finishing straight becomes a sprint finish between a tightly packed field.
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo bunches the entire field, rendering early position irrelevant and turning the race into a two-furlong dash; in this scenario the horse with the sharpest acceleration on good-to-firm — Alfa Whiteburd given her recent winning form — has the edge, though The Good Biscuit's class at the head of affairs keeps her dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Unpicks Race
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group suffers interference or blocked runs in the straight, scrambling the result.
scenarios.body: With so many genuine hold-up types compressed at the rear, sustained traffic problems are a real risk in the final two furlongs; the horses most likely to escape unscathed are those with alert jockeys and wide draws who can find room earliest — Rare Change with Cieren Fallon aboard and Yes I'm Mali are best placed to capitalise if interference scrambles the expected order.

watchPoints.text: Veblen Good sets off alone in front — if she builds even a small buffer before halfway, she may prove very difficult to reel in on good-to-firm ground with no pace rival to soften her up.

The Good Biscuit will be tracking Veblen Good throughout; if she can stay within a length or two turning for home, her prominent position gives her a decisive structural advantage over every hold-up rival in the field.

Alfa Whiteburd arrives in the form of her life with three wins on the bounce, but Jason Hart will need to find a gap smartly in a congested hold-up group — any traffic trouble in the final furlong could cost her the chance her form merits.

With Russet Gold, Havana Rum, Mondammej and Fiscal Policy all genuine hold-up types battling for the same late ground, the straight is likely to see significant crowding — watch for bumping or checked runs among this group from the two-furlong pole.

Rare Change's headgear (hood) is flagged and Cieren Fallon is a shrewd judge of pace — if she travels better than her recent form suggests, she could emerge as the most dangerous hold-up runner of the bunch at a potentially inflated price.
